title: The Art of Silhouette

image.alt: Model in a dark brown tailored suit against a sunlit plaster wall

excerpt: Structure and movement can share one shape. We look at the line a garment draws around the body before fabric or colour arrive.

body.text: Silhouette is the first thing anyone reads. Before fabric or colour, there is the line a garment draws around the body, and this season we wanted that line to feel calm and certain.
A shoulder that holds its edge is the anchor. Around it we let the fabric move: a wide trouser that swings when you walk, a coat cut long enough to keep travelling after you stop.
A good silhouette should look effortless from across the room and considered up close.
Start with one strong shape and keep everything else quiet. A structured blazer over a soft knit, or a fluid trouser under a sharp coat, is often all it takes.
The pieces below are the ones our studio reaches for first.
